title: The rise of Hitler and the Nazis to January 1933

review.note: Original content following 4HI1 Depth study 3, key topic 3. Read more: Payne, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Germany, chapter 3 (pp. 39–59).

learn.intro: How did a small Munich party become the largest in Germany, and how did Hitler become Chancellor in January 1933 without ever winning a majority?

sections.title: 1. Hitler and the early party, 1919–22

blocks.p: Hitler joined the German Workers' Party (DAP), led by Anton Drexler, in September 1919. He was a powerful speaker and soon became its leading figure. In 1920 the party published its 25-Point Programme and renamed itself the National Socialist German Workers' Party (NSDAP), or Nazi Party.

Changes 1920–22: Hitler became party leader in 1921; the party adopted the swastika symbol and bought a newspaper, the Völkischer Beobachter; and the SA (stormtroopers or 'Brownshirts') was set up in 1921, led by Ernst Röhm, to protect Nazi meetings and disrupt opponents'.

evidence: 1921: Hitler becomes leader; SA set up.

blocks.p: Causes: Germans were angry about the Ruhr occupation and hyperinflation; Hitler wanted to copy Mussolini's March on Rome; and the Bavarian government was right-wing, so he hoped its leaders would join him.

Events: on 8 November 1923 Hitler and the SA burst into a meeting at a Munich beer hall and forced the Bavarian leaders Kahr, Lossow and Seisser to support him. They later changed their minds. On 9 November Hitler, with the war hero General Ludendorff, marched into Munich; police opened fire and 16 Nazis were killed.

Results: the Nazi Party was banned and Hitler was put on trial. The trial gave him national publicity; the judge sentenced him to five years but he served only nine months in Landsberg prison, where he wrote Mein Kampf. He decided to win power legally, through elections.

Reorganisation 1924–28: Hitler refounded the party in 1925 and set up branches across Germany run by Gauleiters; the SS was formed as his bodyguard; the Hitler Youth was set up; Joseph Goebbels ran propaganda. But in the stable 'Golden Years' the Nazis won only 12 seats in 1928.

The Great Depression: after the Wall Street Crash (October 1929), American banks recalled their loans. German businesses closed and unemployment rose to 6 million by 1932. Coalition governments could not agree what to do, so Chancellor Brüning ruled by decree using Article 48 and cut spending, which made people suffer more.

Many Germans turned to extreme parties. The Nazis rose from 12 seats (1928) to 107 (1930) and 230 (July 1932), becoming the largest party. The Communists grew too, which frightened the middle classes and business owners.

sections.title: 4. Nazi methods and the role of the SA

ul: Propaganda: Goebbels used posters, newspapers, radio, rallies and films with simple slogans such as 'Work and Bread'.
Hitler's image: a strong leader who would make Germany great again; in 1932 he flew around Germany to speak at rallies.
Promises to everyone: jobs for workers, protection for farmers and small businesses, action against communists for the middle classes and industrialists.
Scapegoats: blaming Jews, communists and the 'November criminals' for Germany's problems.

The SA: hundreds of thousands of Brownshirts marched, protected Nazi meetings and attacked opponents, especially communists, giving an image of order and strength — while causing violence on the streets.

evidence: 1932: Hitler's flights to rallies across Germany.

sections.title: 5. From 1932 to January 1933

blocks.p: In the presidential election of 1932 Hitler won about 13 million votes but lost to Hindenburg. Brüning was replaced by Franz von Papen in May 1932. After the July 1932 election the Nazis were the largest party, but Hindenburg refused to make Hitler Chancellor.

In the November 1932 election the Nazis lost seats (196) and money was running short. Hindenburg appointed General Kurt von Schleicher as Chancellor in December, but he could not win support in the Reichstag.

Papen persuaded Hindenburg to appoint Hitler as Chancellor with Papen as Vice-Chancellor, believing that with only three Nazis in the cabinet they could control him. Hitler became Chancellor on 30 January 1933.

evidence: 1932: Hitler wins about 13 million votes in the presidential election.

A severe economic slump with mass unemployment.

misconceptions.wrong: Hitler was voted in as Chancellor.
misconceptions.right: Hindenburg appointed him; the Nazis never had a majority of votes.

misconceptions.wrong: The Munich Putsch was a total failure for Hitler.
misconceptions.right: It failed as a revolt but the trial made him famous and changed his strategy.

evidence.q: Give precise evidence that the Depression helped the Nazis.
evidence.model: Unemployment rose to 6 million by 1932 and Nazi seats rose from 12 (1928) to 230 (July 1932).

evidence.model: Papen persuaded Hindenburg to appoint Hitler with Papen as Vice-Chancellor and only three Nazis in the cabinet.

flashcards.q: Name two changes to the party in 1920–22.
flashcards.a: Renamed NSDAP; 25-Point Programme; swastika; own newspaper; SA set up; Hitler as leader.

flashcards.q: Give two causes of the Munich Putsch.
flashcards.a: Anger at the Ruhr occupation and hyperinflation; copying Mussolini; hoping Bavarian leaders would join.

flashcards.q: Give two results of the Munich Putsch.
flashcards.a: Party banned; Hitler's trial gave him publicity; Mein Kampf; decision to use elections.
Gauleiters ran regional branches; SS and Hitler Youth set up; Goebbels's propaganda.

flashcards.q: How did the Depression affect Germany?
flashcards.a: US loans recalled; businesses closed; 6 million unemployed by 1932; rule by decree.

flashcards.q: Give three Nazi methods of winning support.
flashcards.a: Propaganda; Hitler's image and rallies; promises to each group; scapegoats; SA marches and violence.

flashcards.q: Why did Papen and Hindenburg appoint Hitler?
flashcards.a: They thought they could control him with only three Nazis in the cabinet, and needed Reichstag support.

I can explain the causes, events and results of the Munich Putsch.
I can explain how the party was reorganised in 1924–28.
I can explain the impact of the Great Depression and Nazi methods, including the SA.
I can judge why Hitler became Chancellor in January 1933, including the roles of Papen, Schleicher and Hindenburg.
